name: Question 5
problem:
$$
P=[\begin{aligned}2 & 4 & 6 \\ -3 & 0 & -2 \\ 1 & 5 & 3\end{aligned}],\,B=[\begin{aligned}-1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 5 & 7 \\ 0 & -7 & 5\end{aligned}]
$$

Consider the nonsingular matrix $P$ and the block diagonal matrix $B$ shown above, where the $2\times 2$ block of $B$ is a rotation-scaling matrix.
Given that $A=PB{P}^{-1},$ what are the complex (not real) eigenvalues and the corresponding eigenvectors of $A?$
worked_solution:
Recall that if $A$ is a $3\times 3$ real matrix that has one real eigenvalue ${\lambda }_{1}$ with corresponding eigenvector ${v}_{1},$ and two complex eigenvalues ${\lambda }_{2}={\overset{―}{\lambda }}_{3}$ with corresponding eigenvectors ${v}_{2}={\overset{―}{v}}_{3},$ then $A=PB{P}^{-1},$ where

$$
B=[\begin{aligned}{\lambda }_{1} & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & \text{Re}({\lambda }_{2}) & \text{Im}({\lambda }_{2}) \\ 0 & -\text{Im}({\lambda }_{2}) & \text{Re}({\lambda }_{2})\end{aligned}],\,\,P=[\begin{aligned}| & | & | \\ {v}_{1} & \text{Re}({v}_{2}) & \text{Im}({v}_{2}) \\ | & | & |\end{aligned}].
$$

Notice that swapping the blocks on the main diagonal of $B$ will result in switching the corresponding columns in $P.$

- From our block diagonal matrix 

$$
B=[\begin{aligned}-1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 5 & 7 \\ 0 & -7 & 5\end{aligned}],
$$

we deduce the complex eigenvalues are ${\lambda }_{2,3}=5\pm 7\text{i}$ and the real eigenvalue is ${\lambda }_{1}=-1.$

- From our matrix 

$$
P=[\begin{aligned}2 & 4 & 6 \\ -3 & 0 & -2 \\ 1 & 5 & 3\end{aligned}],
$$

we deduce that the complex and real eigenvectors are

$$
{v}_{2,3}=[\begin{aligned}4\pm 6\text{i} \\ ∓2\text{i} \\ 5\pm 3\text{i}\end{aligned}],\,{v}_{1}=[\begin{aligned}2 \\ -3 \\ 1\end{aligned}].
$$

Question 5
?

P=[246−30−2153],B=[−1000570−75]

Consider the nonsingular matrix P and the block diagonal matrix B shown above, where the 2×2 block of B is a rotation-scaling matrix. Given that A=PBP−1, what are the complex (not real) eigenvalues and the corresponding eigenvectors of A?

a
λ=−5±i and v=[2±6i∓i3∓5i]
b
λ=5±7i and v=[4±6i∓2i5±3i]
c
λ=−5±7i and v=[−4∓6i∓2i1±5i]
d
λ=7±5i and v=[2±6i±2i3±5i]
e
λ=5±i and v=[−4±6i∓2i5∓3i]
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

Recall that if A is a 3×3 real matrix that has one real eigenvalue λ1 with corresponding eigenvector v1, and two complex eigenvalues λ2=λ―3 with corresponding eigenvectors v2=v―3, then A=PBP−1, where B=[λ1000Re(λ2)Im(λ2)0−Im(λ2)Re(λ2)],P=[|||v1Re(v2)Im(v2)|||]. Notice that swapping the blocks on the main diagonal of B will result in switching the corresponding columns in P.

  • From our block diagonal matrix B=[−1000570−75], we deduce the complex eigenvalues are λ2,3=5±7i and the real eigenvalue is λ1=−1.

  • From our matrix P=[246−30−2153], we deduce that the complex and real eigenvectors are v2,3=[4±6i∓2i5±3i],v1=[2−31].
